design_contribution.title: Boredom-as-lifecycle-observer recontextualization
design_contribution.summary: Boredom should not be a parallel mechanism. It should be one more application of the lifecycle hook idiom (Idiom 4 in CORE_IDIOMS.md): subscribers to a new lifecycle:substrate:idle event, dispatched through the standard recommend → slot-binding → execute pipeline, selecting via Thompson Sampling conditioned on the current ISS/PSS state.
design_contribution.interaction_with_existing_phase_7: Refines Phase 7 (boredom-vessel) scope: vessel becomes just an idle-detection emitter (~50 LOC) + subscription mechanism. No separate boredom registry. No hardcoded goal text or template list.
design_contribution.interaction_with_linchpin_fix: Compatible with and complementary to GOAL_RUNTIME=ias-executor (per dev-guidance-2026-05-24.md). Together: substrate has correct chain propagation across all execution paths (goal-driven AND boredom-driven).
design_contribution.what_this_enables: Substrate develops learned maintenance routines. Thompson posteriors over (boredom_eligible_template, state_space_signature) emerge as the substrate accumulates boredom-fire outcomes. Substrate self-optimizes its idle work.
design_contribution.discovered_during_subagent_research: Current boredom service has evolved past goal-text posting — now enqueues 4 templateIds to a Redis medium-priority queue (per F-024 audit response). The recontextualization still applies because trigger + template-set remain hardcoded.
